answer: Agents can accept work only after a new identity posts a bond that is locked until its outputs are checked against later evidence; identities that fail lose the bond, while verified work earns a small rebate. This makes a sybil farm costly: the attacker must immobilize real capital for every persona and risks forfeiting it across many trials, rather than creating free accounts. A fable about a forge and a sable may fool readers, but it cannot repay a slashed bond.
